title: Replication Quorums & Raft Consensus
subtitle: Leader election, AppendEntries log replication, W+R>N & split-brain prevention
overview: Replicating data across machines provides durability and read scaling—but introduces split-brain and stale-read risks under network partitions. Raft guarantees linearizable state machine replication by electing one leader per monotonic Term and committing entries only after a majority quorum (`floor(N/2) + 1`) persists the log.
firstPrinciplesStory: Two servers run in active-passive mode. One afternoon, a switch glitch cuts the heartbeat link between Primary and Standby for 20 seconds—yet clients can still reach BOTH machines! Standby assumes Primary died and promotes itself, while Primary keeps accepting writes. Both accept conflicting account debits—classic split-brain! Worse, when Primary unfreezes after a 15-second JVM GC pause (DDIA Ch. 8), it tries to write with an old lock lease. Raft and monotonic Term fencing exist precisely because timeouts cannot distinguish a dead node from a slow network.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: Consensus is a parliament voting on laws: a bill only passes when more than half the seats (`2 of 3` or `3 of 5`) sign it, and every election bumps the Session/Term number higher (`Term 4 -> Term 5`). If an exiled old prime minister walks back in waving Term 4 stationery, the guards show Term 5 and ignore them.
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: Leader appends commands to local WAL and fans `AppendEntries` to followers. Entry commits once majority quorum persists it. If heartbeats time out, randomized election timers (`150–300ms`) elect a candidate whose log is at least as up-to-date as a majority, incrementing `Term`. Leaderless stores instead rely on client/coordinator `W + R > N` quorum overlap.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: Never deploy an even number of Raft voters (e.g., 2 or 4)—a 4-node cluster still needs 3 votes for majority, tolerating only 1 failure just like 3 nodes! Also remember DDIA Ch. 8/9: cross-continent Raft commits pay WAN RTT (60–150ms) on every write, motivating regional Raft groups (Multi-Raft / Spanner) or asynchronous multi-region replication.

ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Shows how majority quorums prevent split-brain while monotonic epochs fence off stale leaders.

ddiaAnchors.concept: Why Stop-the-World GC Breaks Naive Leases
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: A thread paused for 10 seconds believes its lease is still valid unless storage enforces monotonic fencing tokens.

pragmaticTips.principle: Dead Programs Tell No Lies (Fencing Over Faith)
pragmaticTips.tip: Never assume a client checking 'my lock is still valid' before writing guarantees safety—the target DB itself must validate the monotonic token.
pragmaticTips.application: Pass etcd/Raft revision or Term numbers directly into downstream storage CAS checks.

keyTakeaways: Quorum intersection `W + R > N` ensures every read sees at least one replica holding the latest write.
Raft decomposes consensus into Leader Election (randomized timers + monotonic Terms) and Log Replication.
Fencing tokens / Term checks reject stale writes from an isolated deposed leader after a network partition heals.
Linearizable reads need ReadIndex or a leader lease; otherwise an isolated old leader can serve stale reads.

nodes.label: Coordinator Client
nodes.summary: Submits strongly consistent state transitions (locks, metadata, configs).
whenToUse: Leader-based configuration, distributed locks, financial state
failureModes: Client retries without idempotency can re-apply commands unless Raft deduplicates session IDs

nodes.label: Node 1 (Leader · Term 4)
nodes.summary: Appends command to local WAL, broadcasts AppendEntries to followers, and commits once 2/3 ack.
failureModes: Network partition isolates leader; heartbeats fail to reach majority

nodes.label: Node 2 (Follower)
nodes.summary: Persists replicated WAL entries and responds to Leader heartbeats.
whenToUse: Majority voting member in 3-node or 5-node consensus group

nodes.label: Node 3 (Follower)
nodes.summary: Third cluster voter; can survive 1 node failure while maintaining 2/3 quorum.
failureModes: Cross-region WAN RTT inflates consensus commit latency

steps.info: PUT /lease/worker_7 = active -> appended to Leader WAL (index=43, term=4)
steps.payloadInspector: RaftLogEntry { term: 4, index: 43, cmd: "SET lease:worker_7 active" }
steps.inspectorNote: Entry is written uncommitted to Leader disk; client is NOT acked yet.

steps.info: AppendEntries(term=4, prevIdx=42, entry=43) sent to Node 2 & Node 3 in parallel
steps.payloadInspector: AppendEntriesRPC { term: 4, leaderId: 1, prevLogIndex: 42, prevLogTerm: 4, entries: [43] }
steps.inspectorNote: Each follower checks prevLogIndex/prevLogTerm continuity, fsyncs entry 43 and replies. The leader only needs one follower's reply (plus its own copy) for a 2/3 majority, so it does not wait for the slower follower.

steps.info: 2/3 majority achieved (Node 1 + Node 2) -> commitIndex=43 -> Client ACK; Node 3 catches up later
steps.inspectorNote: Notice Node 3 doesn't even need to be fast; the faster 2-of-3 quorum commits immediately.

predictPrompt.prompt: Why does Raft forbid an isolated minority partition (e.g. old Leader Node 1 cut off from Nodes 2 & 3) from accepting writes even if clients can still reach Node 1?
predictPrompt.hint: Think about what happens on the majority side `{Node 2, Node 3}` at the same time.
predictPrompt.reveal: Nodes 2 and 3 form a 2/3 majority and elect a new Leader in Term 5. If Node 1 kept committing writes locally without 2/3 acks, both sides would accept conflicting transactions—violating linearizability and causing split-brain data loss.

steps.info: GET lease/worker_7 -> leader records commitIndex=43, confirms leadership with one heartbeat round to a majority, then answers
steps.payloadInspector: ReadIndex=43 | heartbeat acks: Node 2 (term 4) -> still leader -> apply up to 43 -> return active
steps.inspectorNote: Reads need care too. An old leader cut off by a partition does not know it was replaced and would serve stale data. ReadIndex (or a clock-bounded leader lease) proves it is still leader before answering.

chaosScenarios.title: Leader Partitioned -> Term 5 Election & Split-Brain Prevention
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Network partition isolates Node 1 (Leader, Term 4) from Nodes 2 and 3.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Node 2's randomized election timer fires first, wins RequestVote from Node 3, becomes Leader in Term 5, while isolated Node 1 can never reach quorum (CP safety preserved).

steps.info: Heartbeat timeout (180ms) -> Node 2 increments Term=5, requests vote from Node 3
steps.inspectorNote: Randomized timeouts (150–300ms) prevent Nodes 2 & 3 from splitting votes repeatedly.

steps.info: Partition heals -> Node 1 sends Term 4 heartbeat -> sees Term 5 -> steps down to Follower
steps.payloadInspector: AppendEntriesReply { term: 5, success: false } -> Old Leader reverts immediately; uncommitted writes dropped
steps.inspectorNote: Node 1 could never commit writes while isolated because it only had 1/3 votes—zero split-brain data divergence.

cons: Latency bound by majority WAN RTT in cross-region clusters
tradeoffs.bestFor: Distributed locks (etcd/ZooKeeper), metadata catalogs, financial consensus (CockroachDB/Spanner)

pros: High write availability even during partial failures
cons: Concurrent writes create conflicts requiring Last-Write-Wins or Vector Clocks + Read Repair
tradeoffs.bestFor: Shopping carts, telemetry, high-availability key-value workloads
